A lot of professional work around documents can be arbitrarily challenging to automate.

It not only requires deep visual perception/OCR around complex entities (diagrams/charts), but also requires a reasoning trace that can reconcile disparate sources of oftentimes contradictory information. 

Check out the example video below around a water loss audit. Solving this task not only requires reading the water loss diagram, but also understand the exact date and subsequent changes in the appendix.

We think hard document extraction tasks as a microcosm for professional work over PDFs. That's why we launched ExtractBenchPro - a benchmark that's challenging even for the latest frontier models (e.g. Astra/Opus). 

Even as frontier models with max thinking models push the boundaries of accuracy, there is a massive opportunity to build specialized models that can push the frontiers of cost and latency. 

For more info on ExtractBench Pro, check out our blog and the website! https://t.co/bwxs86iS1d

quotedTweet.text:
Introducing ExtractBenchPro: the most challenging benchmark for real-world document extraction.

We see a massive long tail of document complexity in terms of use cases brought on from our customers, that are completely unsolved from a price-performance standpoint. These include trial balances, well logs, canvass binders, site plan reviews, duty reconciliations, loss runs, and more.

Most existing extraction benchmarks are saturated by the frontier models (our cheapest modes now score 93%+ on ExtractBench). So there is enormous economic value in building a complex extraction benchmark that reflects this long-tail of knowledge work.

We spent a long time curating the most complex elements that we saw from real world extraction use cases:
✅ Document conventions: containing legends or rules where the rest of the document should be interpreted
✅ Density of internal jargon: specific definitions that must be cross-referenced within a doc
✅ Aggregation and reasoning: beyond returning exact values on a page, infer values derived from aggregating multiple sources of information
✅ Drawn relations: complex diagrams like procedures and circuits
✅ Charts inside documents: read precise points within a chart
✅ Long chart sheets: some data series like well logs cram all this data into an extremely long page

Within the industries where document extraction is relevant, even small mistakes can have enormous negative impacts. Therefore our headline evaluation metric is based on perfect documents: the proportion of docs with perfect (100%) value f1 score.
(Besides this we also measure value f1 and grounded f1)

It’s an extremely hard task for even the latest frontier models to solve, topping out at ~58% or so in Value F1 score for Codex with Astra - which is quite good but extremely expensive (almost $1 per page!) Our LlamaParse agentic/agentic plus modes are 20-40% and cover the left side of the Pareto frontier, at price ranges that are feasible for full production use.

ExtractBenchPro is available today as a website/technical blog, and also on Github and HuggingFace. Check it out!

推出 ExtractBenchPro：面向真实世界文档提取、挑战性最高的基准测试。

客户带来的应用场景中，存在大量复杂文档的长尾需求，从性价比角度看，这些需求仍完全没有得到解决。例如试算平衡表、测井记录、拉票资料册、场地规划审查、关税对账、理赔历史记录等。

前沿模型在大多数现有提取基准上的表现已接近饱和（我们最便宜的模式如今在 ExtractBench 上也能达到 93% 以上）。因此，构建一个反映这类知识工作长尾需求的复杂提取基准，具有巨大的经济价值。

我们花了很长时间，从真实提取场景中筛选出最复杂的要素：
✅ 文档约定：包含图例或规则，解读文档其余内容时必须遵循
✅ 内部术语密度：包含特定定义，需要在文档内交叉查阅
✅ 汇总与推理：不只是返回页面上的原始数值，还要汇总多个信息来源并推导结果
✅ 图示关系：流程图、电路图等复杂图示
✅ 文档内图表：精确读取图表中的数据点
✅ 超长图表页：测井记录等数据序列会将大量数据塞进极长的单页

在需要文档提取的行业中，即使很小的错误也可能造成严重后果。因此，我们的核心评估指标以完全正确的文档为依据：数值 F1 得分达到满分（100%）的文档占比。
（此外，我们还衡量数值 F1 和有据可依的 F1 得分）

即使对最新的前沿模型而言，这项任务也极其困难。使用 Astra 的 Codex，数值 F1 得分最高也只有约 58%。这个成绩相当不错，但成本极高（每页接近 1 美元！）。我们的 LlamaParse agentic/agentic plus 模式得分为 20%–40%，位于帕累托前沿的低成本一侧，价格适合全面投入生产使用。

posts.text:
Terminal Agent 很容易遇到一种失败是前面修对了 90%，最后一个 hidden test 没过，最终结果还是失败。

这篇 Terminal-RSI 研究的，就是怎么把这种「差一点成功」也变成下一轮真正有用的训练信号。

它交替做两件事。

RSR 会从已经验证成功的轨迹里提炼可复现的做法，再教回 Agent；

RPR 则继续用强化学习消化执行反馈，让局部进展可以获得 credit，同时保证「真正完成任务」始终比只通过部分检查更重要。

论文还有一个很细的设计是 Terminal 里一次命令可能吐出几千 token 日志，但期间 Agent 根本没有做新决策。

所以它把信用分配的时间尺度从「token 数量」改到「交互轮次」，避免日志越长，前面的关键决策反而被稀释。

基于 Qwen3.8-27B，经过两轮 RSR + RPR 后，四个 Terminal-Bench 的平均成功率从 20.68% 提升到 50.58%；Terminal-Bench Hard 从 31% 提升到 79%。

我比较喜欢这篇对「失败轨迹」的处理方式。

一次任务没通过终验，不代表前面所有判断都没有价值。

真正好的自我改进系统，应该能把已经走对的部分留下来，同时知道最后为什么还差那一步。

quotedTweet.text:
Yesterday evening I had the pleasure of attending an interesting event hosted by @sfcompute and @jumptrading focused on the compute space. Some brief takeaways:

- There's an increasing understanding that greater liquidity in compute markets requires the construction of unifying benchmark indices, so that bespoke/OTC markets can be priced/quoted as a diff to a shared set of benchmarks, similar to what exists in the energy complex already (think crude grades and power). Part of the discussion is whether this will organically emerge if more traditional players (Citadel, Jump, blue-chip banks) expand their OTC offering for bilateral hedges (using their own prices), or require an independent party (S&P, CME, etc.) to validate and give credence for broader adoption.

- Massive growth in the compute space is largely underpinned by structured financing trades with hedging mandates (similar to what you see in the oil and gas space). If someone with a sizable balance sheet just lent you a lot of money, who's likely to give you more aggressive pricing than their sales and trading arm?

- Funding from life insurers has been a key part of the data center buildout (you could call it duration matching), with an increasing number of insurers considering hedging compute. Some of this exposure sits in mortgage books, while the biggest bucket is via corporate bonds ($ORCL, $MSFT, $META, and $GOOG comprise nearly 80% of Athene's IG software debt).

- Quite a few folks seem offered over on the backend of the curve, largely driven by:
* Concerns that distressed sellers could flood the market if the AI growth story slows down (as there's a lot of GPU-backed debt to unwind)
* Natural hedgers are mostly sellers, as operators need contracted revenue to borrow, so they sell further out on the curve; buyers mostly lock in near-term rates w/ marginal demand coming from a handful of labs whose spending is contingent on their ability to still tap into financing
* Software improvements are reducing GPU-hour needs, all the while new chips are depreciating the value of old hardware per unit of compute: $NVDA is releasing a new gen roughly every year (Blackwell Ultra, Rubin, and Rubin Ultra). That said, it does look like old chips are staying useful longer than most depreciation models assume, since inference and smaller models still allow sufficient monetization of older hardware.

It'll be quite exciting to see how the space continues to mature, especially as new marketplaces begin to emerge for financially and physically settled compute. Huge thanks to @affaan and team for organizing!
quotedTweet.translationZh:
昨晚很高兴参加了 @sfcompute 和 @jumptrading 举办的一场聚焦算力领域的有趣活动。简单分享几点收获：

- 越来越多人认识到，要提高算力市场的流动性，就需要建立统一的基准指数，让定制化交易和场外交易（OTC）能够参照一套共同基准，以价差形式定价或报价，类似能源市场已有的做法（比如不同品级的原油和电力）。讨论的一个焦点是：如果更多传统机构（Citadel、Jump、大型知名银行）扩大场外业务，按各自报价提供双边对冲，这套基准会自然形成，还是需要独立机构（S&P、CME 等）认证背书，才能得到广泛采用。

- 算力领域的高速增长，很大程度上由附带对冲要求的结构化融资交易支撑，类似油气行业的情况。如果一家资金雄厚的机构刚借给你一大笔钱，还有谁会比它旗下的销售交易部门给你更有竞争力的报价？

- 寿险公司的资金是数据中心建设的重要支撑（可以理解为久期匹配），而且越来越多保险公司正在考虑对冲算力风险。部分相关敞口位于抵押贷款资产组合中，但最大的一块来自公司债券（$ORCL、$MSFT、$META 和 $GOOG 占 Athene 所持投资级软件行业债券的近 80%）。

- 不少人似乎倾向于卖出远期算力，主要原因包括：
* 担心一旦 AI 增长放缓，陷入财务困境的卖家会大量涌入市场，因为有大量以 GPU 为抵押的债务需要清偿。
* 有实际对冲需求的参与者大多是卖方：运营商需要签约收入才能借款，因此会卖出期限更远的算力；买方则主要锁定近期价格，新增需求主要来自少数几家实验室，而它们的支出取决于能否继续获得融资。
* 软件改进正在减少所需的 GPU 小时数，同时新芯片不断拉低旧硬件单位算力的价值：$NVDA 大约每年推出一代新产品（Blackwell Ultra、Rubin 和 Rubin Ultra）。不过，旧芯片的实际可用年限似乎比多数折旧模型假设的更长，因为推理和较小规模的模型仍能让旧硬件产生足够收益。

很期待看到这个领域继续成熟，尤其是随着现金结算和实物交割的算力交易市场陆续出现。非常感谢 @affaan 和团队组织这次活动！

What's still very hard: theory of mind. The world, the voices and the mechanics were great. Writing the story was the weak part: the model assumes the player knows more than they do, and its NPC sometimes react in strange way or to things that never happened.

A Diamond Age's Primer (or any real AI tutor fwiw) will have to model the learner, and that is where it still falls short in a default setting imo. You play the Keeper, and you train Kite, a paper kite with a lantern for a heart. Two keys: T to treat, C to correct. Kite learns from what it was thinking, not just from what it did. Treat Kite for picking fruit while it's thinking about the bell, and the bell-thinking gets stronger too.

That was Claude's design choice, and it's a cartoon of RL: more "clicker training" than actual RLVR. But it gets one thing right: reward the right answer for the wrong reason, and you reinforce the wrong reason.

reviewedPosts.text:
A lot of professional work around documents can be arbitrarily challenging to automate.

It not only requires deep visual perception/OCR around complex entities (diagrams/charts), but also requires a reasoning trace that can reconcile disparate sources of oftentimes contradictory information. 

Check out the example video below around a water loss audit. Solving this task not only requires reading the water loss diagram, but also understand the exact date and subsequent changes in the appendix.

We think hard document extraction tasks as a microcosm for professional work over PDFs. That's why we launched ExtractBenchPro - a benchmark that's challenging even for the latest frontier models (e.g. Astra/Opus). 

Even as frontier models with max thinking models push the boundaries of accuracy, there is a massive opportunity to build specialized models that can push the frontiers of cost and latency. 

For more info on ExtractBench Pro, check out our blog and the website! https://t.co/bwxs86iS1d

Terminal Agent 很容易遇到一种失败是前面修对了 90%，最后一个 hidden test 没过，最终结果还是失败。

这篇 Terminal-RSI 研究的，就是怎么把这种「差一点成功」也变成下一轮真正有用的训练信号。

它交替做两件事。

RSR 会从已经验证成功的轨迹里提炼可复现的做法，再教回 Agent；

RPR 则继续用强化学习消化执行反馈，让局部进展可以获得 credit，同时保证「真正完成任务」始终比只通过部分检查更重要。

论文还有一个很细的设计是 Terminal 里一次命令可能吐出几千 token 日志，但期间 Agent 根本没有做新决策。

所以它把信用分配的时间尺度从「token 数量」改到「交互轮次」，避免日志越长，前面的关键决策反而被稀释。

基于 Qwen3.8-27B，经过两轮 RSR + RPR 后，四个 Terminal-Bench 的平均成功率从 20.68% 提升到 50.58%；Terminal-Bench Hard 从 31% 提升到 79%。

我比较喜欢这篇对「失败轨迹」的处理方式。

一次任务没通过终验，不代表前面所有判断都没有价值。

真正好的自我改进系统，应该能把已经走对的部分留下来，同时知道最后为什么还差那一步。

📎 arxiv: https://t.co/mPakaVb7Sg

学生需要自己设计至少 8 个测试任务，每个跑 3 次，统计成功率、成本和延迟，还得认真分析失败原因。

而且课程的讲义、实验幻灯片和课堂 Demo 都在陆续开源，有源码也有 PDF，很多内容可以直接跟着动手。

感觉这门课挺适合已经在用 Coding Agent、但想把 Agent 工程真正弄明白的人。建议收藏，找时间跟着做一遍。
